1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, melted
• 1 cup granulated sugar
• 2 large eggs
• 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
• 1/3 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
• 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
• 1/4 teaspoon salt
• Optional: 1/2 cup chocolate chips

Instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Line an 8x8-inch baking pan with parchment paper or grease it well.
2. In a large bowl, whisk the melted butter and sugar together until well combined.
3. Add the eggs and vanilla extract. Whisk vigorously for about 1 minute until the mixture is slightly pale and smooth (this helps create that shiny crackly top).
4. Gently fold in the cocoa powder, flour, and salt just until combined. Do not overmix! 
5. Fold in chocolate chips if using.
6. Pour the batter into your prepared pan and spread it into an even layer.
7. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out with a few moist crumbs (but not wet batter).

I love yapping! There's something so deeply satisfying about it - about just talking, letting words spill out, sharing all the random, crazy, and sometimes profound thoughts that pass through my mind. Yapping isn't just a way to communicate; it's a form of expression, an art, a way to connect with others on a level that is often deeper than words alone could ever express. The sheer act of speaking, of letting the thoughts in your head take shape and form in the world outside, is a rush of pure energy.
It's like a continuous flow of electricity, sparking life into the room, into the conversation, into your own existence.
Sometimes, it feels like my mouth has a mind of its own, and before I even know it, I'm caught in the rhythm of words, each one feeding the next in a never-ending loop of exchange and excitement.

Honestly, there's no greater feeling than getting lost in a conversation, when time seems to bend and stretch, and before you know it, hours have passed and you're still talking, still engaging, still diving deeper into ideas, thoughts, and topics that you didn't even think about before the conversation started. Whether it's diving into the latest episode of your favorite show, discussing the latest trends in technology, debating the existence of extraterrestrial life, or just telling some hilarious stories from your childhood, every word, every sentence, builds upon the last, creating this wonderful tapestry of interaction that is always evolving, always growing, always changing.
Yapping isn't just random talking

Yapping isn't just random talking either - no, it's more than that. It's about exploring the infinite possibilities of human connection. It's about finding common ground, discovering new perspectives, challenging old beliefs, and sometimes, just sharing a laugh. How else could we bridge gaps between people of different backgrounds, cultures, and interests if we didn't have the ability to yap? It's how we learn from each other, how we find understanding, how we grow as individuals and as a collective society. With each conversation, we open up new doors, new windows, new paths to knowledge, and we get a little closer to understanding the vastness of the world and the complexities of the human experience.

And don't even get me started on the beauty of a good rant. There's something incredibly freeing about just letting loose, sharing all those frustrations, all those little annoyances that have been building up inside. Yapping can be cathartic - it allows us to vent, to process, to unload the emotional weight that often hangs over us. Sometimes, it's not even about the specific topic being discussed; it's just about the act of expressing ourselves, of making our voices heard, of having someone listen. We all need to feel validated, to feel that what we have to say matters, and there's no better way to experience that than through the simple act of yapping. And while some might dismiss it as "just talking," I believe that there's power in it, that words have the ability to heal, to comfort, to encourage, and to inspire. 

In fact, yapping might just be one of the most underestimated forms of communication.
People think that talking is just a casual thing, but when you really pay attention to the way conversations unfold, you start to see how incredibly important they are. Every word you say, every sentence you string together, has the potential to create change. It could change someone's mood, it could spark an idea, it could shift someone's perspective.
Sometimes, one simple conversation is all it takes to make someone feel seen, heard, or understood, and that's powerful. The ability to connect with another person through words is something that we, as human beings, sometimes take for granted, but it's one of the most magical and essential parts of who we are.

And that's the thing - yapping doesn't have to be profound or life-altering to have an impact.
It doesn't have to be a deep philosophical discussion or a world-changing debate.
Sometimes, the best conversations are the ones that are completely random, the ones where you end up laughing about something silly, the ones where you talk about the most mundane, everyday things, but somehow, in that moment, it feels like the most important thing in the world. Conversations are about more than just exchanging information; they're about creating bonds, sharing experiences, and building memories. It's about finding joy in the little things, whether it's discussing your favorite food, your most recent Netflix binge, or your wildest dreams. There's something deeply comforting in the simple act of sharing thoughts with another person, in knowing that someone else is out there, ready to listen, and ready to engage. 

So, here's to all the yappers out there. The ones who never seem to run out of things to say. The ones who keep the conversations flowing no matter how random, offbeat, or silly they get. We are the ones who make life a little more interesting, a little more vibrant, a little more colorful. We fill the silence with laughter, with stories, with endless streams of words that connect us in ways we may never fully understand. We create the moments that people look back on with a smile, the moments that make them feel connected to the world around them. Yapping is a gift, one that keeps on giving - it never runs out of material, it never gets old, and it never loses its charm.

Because, really, what would life be without yapping? What would we do if we couldn't talk, couldn't share our thoughts and ideas, couldn't laugh or debate or tell stories? Silence is fine for a moment, but it's the chatter, the yapping, the constant hum of conversation that makes the world feel alive. So let's keep on talking, let's keep on sharing, let's keep on yapping, because in the end, it's not just about the words we say - it's about the connections we create, the understanding we foster, and the joy we bring to the world through the simple, beautiful act of conversation. Here's to all the endless, impossible, beautiful yapping that makes life so much richer. May it never stop, may it never end, and may we always have something to say!

To make authentic Italian pizza in 2026, the key is a long cold fermentation process, which develops the complex flavors and airy, digestible crust (cornicione) characteristic of traditional Neapolitan pizza. 
1. Ingredients & Equipment
For the best results, use weight-based measurements and high-heat tools. 
Dough: 500g Tipo "00" flour (or high-protein bread flour), 325ml lukewarm water, 10g sea salt, and 1g–7g of yeast depending on your timeline.
Toppings: Crushed San Marzano tomatoes, fresh mozzarella (fior di latte or buffalo), fresh basil, and extra virgin olive oil.
Tools: A pizza stone or steel is essential for home ovens to mimic a professional deck. 
2. The Multi-Day Dough Process
Mixing: Dissolve salt in water, then add yeast and about 10% of the flour to protect the yeast from direct salt contact. Gradually add the remaining flour.
Kneading: Knead for 10–15 minutes until the dough is smooth and passes the "windowpane test" (stretching thin enough to see light through without tearing).
Bulk Ferment: Let the dough rest in an oiled bowl at room temperature for 2 hours until doubled.
Cold Fermentation: Divide the dough into balls (approx. 250g each), place in sealed containers, and refrigerate for 24 to 72 hours. This "maturation" breaks down complex sugars for better flavor and digestibility.
Final Proof: Remove dough from the fridge 2 hours before baking to reach room temperature. 
3. Stretching and Topping
The Stretch: Dust your surface with semolina flour to prevent sticking. Press from the center outward with your fingertips to push air into the rim. Never use a rolling pin, as it collapses the air bubbles needed for a puffy crust.
Applying Toppings: Spread a thin layer of sauce (you should still "see through" it) and add toppings sparingly. Too many toppings will make the dough soggy. 
4. Baking Techniques
Preheat: Heat your oven to its maximum setting (typically 500–550°F / 260–290°C) with the stone or steel inside for at least 45–60 minutes.
The Broiler Method: For a professional char, set the oven to "Broil" just before launching the pizza.
Baking: Slide the pizza onto the hot stone. In a standard oven, it takes 6–10 minutes. In a dedicated pizza oven (like an Ooni), it takes only 60–90 seconds at 750°F+.
Finish: Add fresh basil and a final drizzle of olive oil after baking to preserve their fresh aroma.

The main reason people hate this update is that, by separating people into age groups, it heavily restricts who you can talk to. This is a good solution in theory, as it helps prevents older malicious people from using the site to funnel younger people to external sites, mainly Discord (think about how many predator catchers and expose videos happen to use or involve discord). Now the issue is, well, if people want to communicate with more people, but can’t on Roblox, where are they going to go? Well, Discord. And where do the malicious people want to take them to? Discord. This is why I believe this might be worse for the platform overall, as it’s pushing people to seek other forms to communicate with each other and leading them to Discord, where there is a lot more danger than on Roblox. Murder Drones is a sci-fi animated web series created by Liam Vickers and produced by GLITCH, known for its unique blend of dark comedy, action, and emotional storytelling. The series is set on Copper-9, a remote, icy planet where humanity once sent Worker Drones to mine resources. After humans mysteriously disappear, these robots are left to survive on their own, only to face a new threat: elite killer drones sent to exterminate them. The story balances horror, humor, and drama while exploring the mysteries of the drones’ world.
The main antagonists are the Disassembly Drones, sleek, winged machines designed purely for killing. Their mission is to locate and destroy every Worker Drone on Copper-9. Despite being built for violence, each Disassembly Drone has a distinct personality, which adds complexity to their interactions. Among them, N stands out as an unexpected ally. Polite, awkward, and compassionate, N begins questioning the purpose he was programmed for, which gradually shifts the balance of power on the planet.
Uzi Doorman, the series’ protagonist, is a rebellious Worker Drone who resents the underground society that hides in fear. She wants to fight back and prove that Worker Drones deserve freedom rather than extermination. Her intelligence, bravery, and sarcasm make her a formidable character, driving much of the series’ action. Uzi’s defiance against both her society and the Disassembly Drones forms the core of the narrative.
Her relationship with her father, Khan Doorman, adds emotional depth. Khan is protective and cautious, wanting to shield Uzi from danger. This tension between parental care and Uzi’s desire for independence explores themes of family, growth, and identity, shaping her journey throughout the series.
A key element in the story is the Absolute Solver, a mysterious and dangerous technological parasite that Uzi encounters. This power amplifies her abilities but also threatens to consume her identity. The Solver’s influence is central to the conflict on Copper-9, connecting Worker and Disassembly Drones and revealing deeper mysteries about the planet’s past and humanity’s downfall.
The series gradually unveils the origins of both Worker and Disassembly Drones and the destructive influence of the Absolute Solver. It introduces cosmic-horror elements that suggest the events on Copper-9 are part of a larger, more catastrophic story. These plot threads add layers of intrigue and raise the stakes beyond mere survival.
V, one of the Disassembly Drones, is a complex antagonist whose personality evolves over time. Initially ruthless and violent, V’s backstory and her interactions with N and J reveal vulnerabilities, making her one of the series’ most compelling characters. This depth blurs the line between hero and villain, keeping the narrative unpredictable.
The worldbuilding in Murder Drones is rich and immersive, combining dystopian sci-fi with horror. The animation style emphasizes expressive character designs and stylized combat sequences, while the tone fluctuates between dark humor, emotional drama, and intense action. This combination has earned the series a passionate fanbase.
At its core, Murder Drones explores themes of identity, purpose, and self-determination. Characters struggle to break free from literal and metaphorical programming, making choices in a world built on fear and destruction. The series uses its robotic characters to examine what it means to be alive and to grow.
Ultimately, Murder Drones is more than a story about killer robots and survival. It is a narrative about relationships, morality, and the consequences of power. Through its evolving characters, intricate lore, and emotional arcs, the series continues to captivate audiences while steadily expanding the mysteries of Copper-9 and the true purpose behind the Absolute Solver.

This whole system is flawed on so many levels. I'm not even going to mention all the chatting issues for proper communications, those have been well pointed out by now.

1. Trusted connections are worthless. If you can use a QR code to bypass the chat, bad actors are just going to ask the other party to "go into Roblox and scan the QR code I'm giving you, so we can talk on Roblox". Phone contacts are an idea but they need to have an NFC lock or something, or bluetooth, something that requires 2 people to be close.

2. The selfie verification, besides being wrong at times, can also be faked. Not only by allowing someone else to do it, but also using pre-recorded videos of others doing it. Nothing prevents you from playing back a recording on like a tablet, or even your computer screen, and just holding your phone in place in order to scan it, rather than a real person.
AI might be able to detect it, but I don't trust them to be able to filter out those mistakes either.

3. Bad actors can just make several alternate accounts in different age classifications and pick and choose what they need. If they just have a range of accounts across all age ranges, they can just choose for every scenario which account they'd need. Let's say they meet someone who is 14, they'll just send them the appropriate Roblox account which they made in that age range to be able to chat them as normal.

4. This will never solve the issue of bad actors getting into contact with people over Discord or other platforms. Granted, Roblox can't do much about this and is basicaly out of their control, however they can properly implement these checks to make it next to impossible to let the issues boil over onto Roblox. Roblox shouldn't be responsible for what happens on Discord though, that's Discord their issue, provided it doesn't boil over into Roblox.

5. Registered content creators (maybe those in the star program only, because they're vetted by Roblox) should be opted out to this system so they can talk with their communities of all ages. These people are vetted by Roblox already, so it's known who they are and that they generally should be trustworthy.

6. All of this requires game creators to utilize the Roblox chat system and content filtering API's. Whilst Roblox will crack down on games that don't use this system and make bypass chat systems, by the time they find the game, it can already be too late. It requires a level of trust from every developer to also follow the imposed rules of the platform on a game level itself, which isn't always being strictly followed either.

I'm not necessarily against the changes Roblox is proposing, I do think it'll improve security. However the way they're going about it is not secure enough to prevent these issues from taking place.
